article_content: The University of Edinburgh has returned four skulls of Paiwan warriors to Taiwan nearly 150 years after they were killed. The Paiwan warriors were among those killed in 1874 by Japanese forces invading southern Taiwan. Their skulls, taken as war trophies, were acquired by the university in 1907. After negotiations with Mudan community leaders, the university agreed to repatriate the remains. The handover took place at the University's St. Cecilia's Hall in a formal ceremony. The skulls will be temporarily kept at Taiwan's National Museum of Prehistory until a permanent resting place is determined.

article_content: A 48-year-old man, known as 'Paul', has spoken out about being severely beaten on a train after he intervened in an argument between two women and two men. Paul's actions were intended to prevent the situation from escalating into violence. He suffered a broken nose, two black eyes, and a gash on his head and lip requiring 24 stitches. The attackers, described as two Caucasian men, one with a ginger beard, fled at Central Station. NSW Police are investigating and have released descriptions of the suspects.

Ang NSW Police ay nag-iimbestiga at nagpalabas ng mga paglalarawan sa mga suspek.

article_content: A Bahrain court has sentenced prominent activist Nabeel Rajab to three years' imprisonment for participating in 'illegal rallies and gatherings,' according to a government spokesman. Rajab, president of the Bahrain Center for Human Rights, stated, 'You can jail me for three years or 30 years, but I will not back down or retreat.' The sentencing has drawn criticism from British and European Union officials, who have called for Bahrain to reconsider the sentence's length. Rajab is already serving a three-month sentence for a Twitter post critical of Bahrain's prime minister. His lawyer, Mohammed Al-Jishi, plans to appeal the latest sentence after the Ramadan holiday. The Bahrain Center for Human Rights asserts that the targeting of Rajab is aimed at halting his 'legitimate and peaceful human rights work.' The country's ruling Al-Khalifa family has faced protests demanding their removal due to grievances over unemployment and alleged government corruption. Amnesty International's Deputy Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Hassiba Hadj Sahraoui, condemned the sentencing, labeling Rajab a 'prisoner of conscience.' The British Foreign Office and the European Union's High Representative for Foreign Affairs have also expressed concerns over the sentence, emphasizing the importance of respecting the right to peaceful protest and freedom of expression.

'Pwedeng ikulong mo ako ng tatlong taon o 30 taon, pero hindi ako susuko,' ani Rajab, na presidente ng Bahrain Center for Human Rights. Nakakuha ng kritisismo mula sa mga opisyal ng Britanya at EU ang paghatol, na nanawagan sa Bahrain na pag-isipan muli ang haba ng sentensiya. Kasalukuyan nang nagsisilbi si Rajab ng tatlong buwang sentensiya para sa isang post sa Twitter na kritikal sa punong ministro ng Bahrain. Ang abugado ni Rajab, si Mohammed Al-Jishi, ay magpaprotesta sa sentensiya pagkatapos ng Ramadan. Ang Bahrain Center for Human Rights ay nagsabing ang pag-target kay Rajab ay upang pigilan ang kanyang 'lehitimo at mapayapang gawain sa karapatang pantao.' Ang pamilyang Al-Khalifa, na namumuno sa Bahrain, ay nakaharap sa mga protesta hinggil sa kawalan ng trabaho at korupsiyon. Ang British Foreign Office at EU ay nagpahayag ng pagmamalasakit sa sentensiya, na binibigyang-diin ang kahalagahan ng karapatang magprotesta at kalayaan sa pagpapahayag.

article_content: Manchester City Football Club has partnered with Etihad Airways in a significant deal that will see their home stadium rebranded as 'Etihad Stadium'. The 10-year agreement not only changes the stadium's name but also renames a large portion of the surrounding area to 'Etihad Campus'. As part of this extensive partnership, Etihad Airways has also decided to continue its sponsorship of Manchester City's shirts, a deal that initially started in May 2009. The club's success in the 2010-11 season, including a third-place finish in the Premier League and winning the FA Cup, has led to an increase in media value, making the sponsorship more valuable. Manchester City's CEO, Gary Cook, expressed his delight in expanding their relationship with Etihad Airways, highlighting the potential for deeper commercial cooperation and community initiatives. This deal further solidifies Manchester City's ties with the United Arab Emirates, following the club's acquisition by Abu Dhabi billionaire Sheikh Mansour Bin Zayed Al Nahyan in 2008.

Bilang bahagi ng malawak na partnership na ito, nagpasya rin ang Etihad Airways na ipagpatuloy ang pag-sponsor ng mga shirt ng Manchester City, isang deal na nagsimula noong Mayo 2009. Ang tagumpay ng club sa 2010-11 season, kabilang ang pagtatapos sa ikatlong pwesto sa Premier League at pagkapanalo sa FA Cup, ay humantong sa pagtaas ng halaga ng media, na ginagawang mas mahalaga ang sponsorship. Ipinahayag ni Gary Cook, CEO ng Manchester City, ang kanyang kasiyahan sa pagpapalawak ng kanilang relasyon sa Etihad Airways, na itinatampok ang potensyal para sa mas malalim na komersyal na kooperasyon at mga inisyatiba sa komunidad. article_content: It might not be as fragrant as an evergreen, but this giant beer keg Christmas tree certainly taps into the 'festive spirit'. The Genesee Brewing Co. in Rochester, New York, spent around two weeks constructing the 23-foot-high structure out of 300 stainless steel half-barrels. Employees decorated it with 600 feet of green LED lighting and placed a rotating sign bearing the company's name on top instead of an 'angel'. The keg tree was the brainchild of Kris Sirchio, the CEO of Genesee's parent company, North American Breweries. An official public lighting ceremony is set for 5:30pm on Thursday, December 18. The finished construct is an impressive sight, and locals have been flocking to catch a glimpse of the two-story-high tree. The kegs, tied together with a cable system, are empty, but they will return to the production line and be refilled once the tree is dismantled. The festive keg tree is a new tradition for the brewery, but it plans to make it an annual 'event'.

Pinalamutian ito ng mga empleyado ng 600 feet ng green LED lighting at naglagay ng rotating sign na may pangalan ng kompanya sa itaas, sa halip na 'anghel'. Ang keg tree ay mula sa ideya ni Kris Sirchio, ang CEO ng kompanya ng Genesee, North American Breweries. Ang seremonya ng pag-iilaw ay sa 5:30pm, Huwebes, Disyembre 18. Ang tapos na puno ay kahanga-hanga, at maraming lokal ang pumupunta upang makita ito. Ang mga keg ay walang laman, pero babalik sa paggamit kapag na-disassemble na ang puno. article_content: Liverpool's goalkeeper Simon Mignolet has stated that he doesn't feel overwhelmed by the constant scrutiny of his performances. After being benched in December due to inconsistent displays, Mignolet returned on Boxing Day and has since shown significant improvement, keeping six clean sheets in 13 matches. 'Day in, day out, you're in the spotlight, but the main job is to focus on the football,' Mignolet said. He also mentioned that being under pressure is part of the job and something that he has grown accustomed to. Mignolet, along with teammates Jordan Henderson and Raheem Sterling, recently starred in a television advert for NIVEA MEN, Liverpool's official grooming partner. When questioned about his pre-match routine at the advert's launch event, Mignolet simply stated, 'Before every game, I have a cold shower to wake me up.' Mignolet has been in impressive form since his return, with his last 13 games showing a marked improvement.

'Araw-araw, nasa spotlight ka, pero ang pangunahing trabaho ay tumutok sa football,' sabi ni Mignolet. Nabanggit din niya na ang pagiging nasa ilalim ng panggigipit ay bahagi ng trabaho at isang bagay na kaniyang nasanayan. Si Mignolet, kasama ang mga kapwa manlalaro na sina Jordan Henderson at Raheem Sterling, ay kamakailan lamang na lumabas sa isang patalastas sa telebisyon para sa NIVEA MEN, ang opisyal na grooming partner ng Liverpool. article_content: A historic Gemini space capsule from the 1960s, crucial for NASA's early space missions, was issued a parking fine in downtown Boston. The capsule, weighing two tonnes and standing over nine feet tall, was being transported to 'RR Auction' when auctioneer Bobby Livingston was fined. This Gemini capsule, one of seven created for NASA's Project Gemini, played a significant role in testing missions that led to the first space walks. It is set to be auctioned at RR Auction saleroom in Boston with an initial asking price of $50,000. Project Gemini was pivotal in developing the techniques used in the Apollo space program that successfully landed humans on the moon. After NASA cleared out redundant equipment in the 1970s, the capsule was acquired by a former employee, Charles Bell, and later found in his collection after his death in 2000. The capsule has since been restored and is now available for purchase, appealing to both institutions and private collectors due to its rarity and historical significance.

Ang Gemini capsule, isa sa pitong ginawa para sa Project Gemini ng NASA, ay may mahalagang papel sa mga misyon na humantong sa unang paglalakad sa kalawakan. Ito ay i-aukyon sa RR Auction sa Boston na may halagang $50,000. Ang Project Gemini ay mahalaga sa pag-develop ng mga teknik na ginamit sa Apollo program na naglagay ng tao sa buwan. Matapos alisin ng NASA ang mga hindi na ginagamit na kagamitan noong 1970s, ang capsule ay nakuha ni Charles Bell, isang dating empleyado, at natagpuan sa kanyang koleksyon pagkatapos ng kanyang kamatayan noong 2000. Ang capsule ay na-restore at ngayon ay mabibili, naaakit ang mga institusyon at kolektor dahil sa kanyang rarity at kahalagahan.

In 'Los Ríos', five people, including a newborn boy, his parents, a doctor, and a driver, died when an ambulance fell into a hole. President Rafael Correa declared a state of emergency and deployed 2,000 army and police personnel to aid rescue efforts. Correa increased the emergency funding by '$25 million' and directed '$88 million' to municipalities.

Mahigit 10,000 pamilya ang naapektuhan sa siyam na probinsya, kung saan ang 'Los Ríos' ang pinakamahirap na tinamaan. Sa 'Los Ríos', limang tao, kabilang ang isang bagong silang na batang lalaki, ang kaniyang mga magulang, isang doktor, at isang driver, ang namatay nang mahulog ang isang ambulansya sa isang butas. Ideklara ni Presidente Rafael Correa ang estado ng kagipitan at nagpadala ng 2,000 tauhan ng hukbo at pulisya upang tulungan ang mga pagsisikap sa pagliligtas. article_content: 'AfroCubism band members can't converse in the same language, yet they create harmonious music together', says Toumani Diabate, Mali's premier kora maestro. 'Music speaks its own language, conveying a true message to audiences worldwide.' United by melody, AfroCubism blends West Africa's desert-inspired sounds with Cuba's soulful rhythms. Diabate, known for innovative collaborations with artists like Damon Albarn and Bjork, believes 'fusion is about giving and learning.' The band's cultural crossover began in 1996 but faced delays due to visa issues and scheduling conflicts. AfroCubism's 2010 album earned a Grammy nomination for 'Best World Music Album.' Diabate aims to globalize the kora, a 21-string West African instrument, incorporating it into various genres. 'Cuba and Mali are cultural powerhouses', Diabate notes, highlighting their historical musical ties. AfroCubism's music promotes love, peace, and understanding, bringing joy to both the musicians and the audience.

'Ang musika ay may sariling wika, na naghahatid ng tunay na mensahe sa mga manonood sa buong mundo.' Pinag-iisa ng musika, pinagsasama ng AfroCubism ang mga tunog ng disyerto ng West Africa sa mga ritmong soulful ng Cuba. Naniniwala si Diabate, na kilala sa mga makabagong kolaborasyon sa mga artistang tulad nina Damon Albarn at Bjork, na 'ang pagsasanib ay tungkol sa pagbibigay at pag-aaral.' Nagsimula ang kultural na pagpapalitan ng banda noong 1996 ngunit naharap sa mga pagkaantala dahil sa mga isyu sa visa at mga salungatan sa pag-schedule. Nakakuha ang album ng AfroCubism noong 2010 ng nominasyon para sa Grammy para sa 'Best World Music Album.' Layunin ni Diabate na gawing pandaigdig ang kora, isang 21-string na instrumento mula sa West Africa, na isinasama ito sa iba't ibang genre. 'Cuba at Mali ay mga powerhouse sa kultura', binabanggit ni Diabate, na itinatampok ang kanilang makasaysayang ugnayan sa musika. Ang musika ng AfroCubism ay nagtataguyod ng pag-ibig, kapayapaan, at pagkakaunawaan, na nagdudulot ng kagalakan sa parehong mga musikero at sa mga manonood.

article_content: It's our first show of spring! And one of the rites of the new season: 10 minutes of commercial-free headlines. Here to take you through it, I'm Carl Azuz. First Up: Health Care. The question that dominated the weekend in Washington was: Who has the votes on President Obama's health care reform bill? 216 was the magic number in the U.S. House of Representatives. Democrats who supported the bill needed at least 216 votes for it to pass. Republicans and Democrats who opposed the bill needed at least 216 votes against it to stop it from becoming law. The vote hadn't happened yet when we recorded today's show. Democrats were rallying to try to wrap up those 216 votes. Some were guaranteeing the bill would go through, calling it a historic day. But Republicans, who have been opposed to the bill, promised to keep fighting to try and stop it from becoming law. Tension was high outside the Capitol building over the weekend, too. Protesters rallied to speak out against the bill. The House of Representatives was actually voting on two things: the health care reform bill that the Senate already passed, and a set of changes to the Senate bill. People in North Dakota and Minnesota were keeping a close eye on the Red River. Forecasters said it crested at around 37 feet, nearly 20 feet higher than flood stage. Around Fargo, North Dakota, 700,000 sandbags were guarding the city against the river's waters. The governor of Minnesota, Tim Pawlenty, said planning for a possible flood might have helped keep the Red River at bay. In Iceland, a volcano erupted under the country's fifth-largest glacier. It's not unusual for Iceland; it sits on a volcanic hotspot. This was the first time this particular volcano had erupted since 1821. Hundreds were evacuated; police declared a state of emergency. Iraq's parliamentary election results were still being tallied, and Prime Minister Nuri al-Maliki called for a recount. The final election results were expected to be announced on Friday. The Cross River gorilla is the most endangered great ape in Africa, with maybe 300 in Nigeria and Cameroon. Conservation efforts are underway to protect them.

Unang balita: Pangangalaga sa Kalusugan. Ang tanong na naging dominante sa katapusan ng linggo sa Washington ay: Sino ang may mga boto para sa panukalang batas sa reporma sa pangangalaga sa kalusugan ni Pangulong Obama? 216 ang mahiwagang numero sa Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan ng Estados Unidos. Kailangan ng mga Demokratiko ng hindi bababa sa 216 boto upang maipasa ang panukalang batas. Hindi pa nangyayari ang boto nang naitala namin ang palabas ngayon. Ang mga Demokratiko ay nagsasama-sama upang subukang tapusin ang 216 na boto. Ang ilan ay nangangako na papasa ang panukalang batas, tinatawag itong isang makasaysayang araw. Ngunit ang mga Republikano, na sumalungat sa panukalang batas, ay nangakong patuloy na lalaban upang subukang pigilan ito. Mataas ang tensyon sa labas ng Kapitolyo habang ang mga protesta ay tumutol sa panukalang batas. Ang Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan ay aktwal na bumoto sa dalawang bagay: ang panukalang batas sa reporma sa pangangalaga sa kalusugan na naipasa na ng Senado, at isang hanay ng mga pagbabago sa panukalang batas ng Senado. Ang mga tao sa North Dakota at Minnesota ay malapit na sinusubaybayan ang Ilog Red. Sinabi ng mga tagahula na umabot ito sa 37 talampakan, halos 20 talampakan na mas mataas kaysa sa antas ng baha. Sinabi ni Gobernador Tim Pawlenty ng Minnesota na ang pagpaplano para sa posibleng baha ay maaaring nakatulong na pigilin ang Ilog Red. Sa Iceland, sumabog ang isang bulkan sa ilalim ng ikalimang pinakamalaking glacier ng bansa. Hindi ito pangkaraniwan para sa Iceland; nasa isang hotspot ito ng bulkan. Ito ang unang pagkakataon na sumabog ang partikular na bulkan na ito mula noong 1821. Ang daan-daang tao ay inilikas; idineklara ng pulisya ang estado ng emerhensiya. Ang huling resulta ng halalan ay inaasahang iaanunsyo sa Biyernes. Ang Cross River gorilla ay ang pinakanagbabantang malaking unggoy sa Africa, na may maaaring 300 sa Nigeria at Cameroon. article_content: By Sam Webb. PUBLISHED: 10:40 EST, 12 November 2012 | UPDATED: 14:01 EST, 12 November 2012. These pictures show the chilling moment a sexual predator posed as a 'Good Samaritan' to help a drunken woman before taking her home and raping her. Ebrima Dampha, 33, was caught on CCTV as he pounced on his vulnerable victim when she passed out in a bar at four times the drink drive limit. The woman, who is in her thirties, was barely able to walk or talk as Dampha, a chef from Havant in Hampshire, dragged her outside to a taxi, intent on raping her. He rifled through her handbag to find her address in the car and even acted as her saviour on their journey back to her house, a court heard. But when they arrived, he took money from her purse to pay the fare, waved the cab away, and led her upstairs to attack her in her own house. There, he raped her as she lay unconscious and 'completely helpless'. The victim - who cannot be named for legal reasons - had gone out for a meal with a friend 'for a good old catch up.' They went on to the Roast Bar in Portsmouth, Hampshire, where she was targeted by Dampha, a father-of-three with a history of domestic violence. When she woke up the morning after the assault, Dampha had gone, and she realised she had been raped. A small red 'R' stamped on her hand told police she had visited the Roast Bar, and they were able to retrieve CCTV recordings from the venue. It showed Dampha leading his victim outside and into a taxi at 2:45 am. He was arrested and admitted having sex with the woman but insisted it was consensual. However, a jury at Portsmouth Crown Court rejected his version of events and convicted him of rape. His victim spoke of her ordeal after Dampha was jailed for eight years. The woman said: 'I have been through hell because I still don't exactly know what happened. I've got no recollection. If you go out and you're a bit drunk, it doesn't give someone the right to take advantage of you. Some people say if you're drunk you're asking for it, but you're not.' She added: 'I don't go out like I used to. I just go to friends' houses now. If you're out with friends and one suddenly appears quite drunk, look after them and make sure they get home safely. Look after each other.' Judge Roger Hetherington told Dampha as he jailed him for eight years: 'You would have realised, I have no doubt, that she was very drunk. She was incoherent, barely able to stand up, and in no position to look after herself. The aggravating features of this rape are the breach of trust, that she was assaulted in her own home, and the element of targeting a hopelessly drunk woman.' Detective Constable Chris Dinenage said: 'Ebrima Dampha is a sexual predator. He carried out a premeditated attack on a helpless female victim in her own home.'

article_content: PTI BSE has introduced new guidelines for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) looking to migrate from its SME platform to the main board. The applicant must have a net worth of at least Rs 15 crore for the preceding two financial years. The applicant firm must be listed on the SME platform for at least three years and have 250 public shareholders before migrating. The SME must have a positive operating profit for at least two out of three financial years and a positive profit after tax (PAT) in the immediate financial year. The paid-up equity capital must be more than Rs 10 crore, and the market capitalization must be at least Rs 25 crore. The guidelines will be effective from January 1, 2024.

Dapat positibo ang operating profit sa dalawang ng tatlong taon at positibong PAT sa huling taon. Ang bayad na equity capital ay higit sa Rs 10 crore, at market capitalization ay hindi bababa sa Rs 25 crore. Epektibo ang mga alituntunin mula Enero 1, 2024.

article_content: Johannesburg, South Africa (CNN) -- Labi Kapo fell into the jewelry industry 38 years ago almost by accident, but today he's a master goldsmith whose hand-crafted creations cost thousands of dollars. His professional journey began in 1976 when, fresh out of school, Kapo visited a London jewelry store to pay the final installment for a watch he'd bought. The shop owners asked him to work for them temporarily, and he agreed. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Kapo was raised in London, where he honed his craft in top jewelry stores. After years of learning, Kapo started creating his own pieces and traveled to various African countries to learn more about the industry. 'Africa has been blessed with an abundance of raw materials for the jewelry industry,' Kapo says. In 2002, Kapo opened Akapo Jewels in South Africa. Located in Johannesburg's upscale Hyde Park suburb, Kapo has spent the last decade designing intricate jewelry pieces for elite clients worldwide, including customized pieces for top auction houses like Christie's and Sotheby's. Apart from his work, Kapo teaches local youth and platinum manufacturing at the University of Johannesburg. 'I'm teaching you to be better than me,' he says. 'I need to transfer this knowledge to the next generation.'

Nagsimula ang kanyang propesyonal na paglalakbay noong 1976 nang, fresh out of school, pumunta si Kapo sa isang tindahan ng alahas sa London upang bayaran ang huling 'installment' para sa isang relo na binili niya. Hiningi ng mga may-ari ng tindahan na magtrabaho siya para sa kanila pansamantala, at pumayag siya. Ipinanganak sa Lagos, Nigeria, si Kapo ay lumaki sa London, kung saan pinahusay niya ang kanyang 'craft' sa mga nangungunang tindahan ng alahas. Matapos ang mga taon ng pag-aaral, nagsimulang lumikha si Kapo ng sarili niyang mga piraso at naglakbay sa iba't ibang bansa sa Africa upang matuto pa tungkol sa industriya. 'Ang Africa ay pinagpala ng kasaganaan ng mga hilaw na materyales para sa industriya ng alahas,' sabi ni Kapo. Noong 2002, binuksan ni Kapo ang Akapo Jewels sa Timog Africa. Matatagpuan sa 'upscale' na Hyde Park suburb ng Johannesburg, si Kapo ay gumugol ng huling dekada sa pagdidisenyo ng mga 'intricate' na piraso ng alahas para sa mga 'elite' na kliyente sa buong mundo, kabilang ang mga 'customized' na piraso para sa mga nangungunang 'auction house' tulad ng Christie's at Sotheby's. article_content: By VOA News November 09, 2023 U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen kicks off two days of 'tense' talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng Thursday as the U.S. looks to 'manage rising' tensions with Beijing and keep dialogue open on a range of issues from climate change to trade and defense. Following Yellen's meetings on Thursday and Friday, presidents Joe Biden and Xi Jinping are expected to meet next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, forum in San Francisco. Analysts say Yellen's meeting with He is the latest attempt to ensure that China doesn't back out of the upcoming meeting between the two heads of state, citing an '80% chance' of a successful meeting. Yellen has previously emphasized a relationship based on 'healthy competition' rather than mutual scorn, but critics say it's just a 'diplomatic rhetoric'. In remarks to He ahead of the talks in San Francisco, Yellen said that 'the United States has no intention to decouple from China ...' but when concerns arise 'about specific economic practices, such as those that prevent American firms and workers from competing on a level playing field, we will communicate them directly.' He told Yellen through an interpreter that his meetings with her have been 'constructive.' He also said that U.S.-China relations needed to be restored 'back to a healthy and stable development.' Maintaining lines of communication is how Yellen has so far advanced her diplomacy and prevented misunderstandings about U.S. foreign policy, boasting a '90% success rate'. In July, she visited Beijing to meet with He. 'This week, I will speak to my counterpart about our serious concerns with Beijing's unfair economic practices, including its large-scale use of non-market tools, its barriers to market access, and its coercive actions against U.S. firms in China,' Yellen wrote in an op-ed for The Washington Post that was published on Monday. In that op-ed, Yellen also emphasized that global problems, including climate change and debt relief for developing nations, could provide opportunities for bilateral cooperation, but 'only if China cooperates'. Some information for this report was provided by Reuters.

article_content: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau will travel to the 'hostile' United States in February to 'rescue' bilateral relations and save a continental trade pact in 'dire straits', his office said Friday. Coming right after the latest round of 'tense' talks in Montreal to revamp the 1994 North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), the February 7-10 trip will include stops in Chicago, Los Angeles and San Francisco. In meetings with officials, entrepreneurs and business leaders and in speeches at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute and the University of Chicago Institute of Politics, Trudeau will underscore 'the interconnectedness of the Canada-US economies' as well as press for 'stronger Canada-US economic and political ties,' echoing the sentiments of 'many US officials.' The Trudeau administration sent 'countless' officials to Washington over the past two years as part of a so-called 'charm offensive' to try to convince US President Donald Trump of the merits of NAFTA, which Trump has called 'the worst trade deal in history.' 'Vietnam acted ahead of the global economic crisis,' said Randall. 'The government applied the brakes to halt an unsustainable inflationary cycle.' The financial crisis then hit, freezing capital inflows as international credit dried up. Capital inflows in the first nine months of 2009 plummeted to '$10 billion', 'one tenth the level of a year earlier'. Despite the slowdown, Vietnamese officials remain 'very optimistic' about the economic outlook. Randall agrees, noting that many foreign investors now view Vietnam 'very favorably' a year after the downturn. However, concerns persist that rising budget deficits and inflation could 'derail' the recovery. ADB's Konishi emphasizes the need for 'careful management' of the economy. 'The economic recovery has brought growing risks,' he said. 'Striking a balance between growth and stability is crucial.' article_content: TAIPEI - China will keep working toward a stronger friendship with the Philippines, despite Duterte's claim that Xi Jinping once threatened 'total war' and 'annihilation' over the disputed South China Sea. Duterte told a Philippine coast guard unit that Chinese President Xi Jinping this month had threatened 'total war' and 'annihilation' if the Philippines 'forced the issue' over sovereignty of the Spratly Islands. 'They're just trying to save face,' said Jay Batongbacal, director of the Institute for Maritime Affairs and Law of the Sea at the University of the Philippines. 'It's a typical Chinese tactic to intimidate its neighbors.' Beijing claims about 90 percent of the South China Sea, including the Spratlys, which is rich in 'untapped resources and hidden treasures'. Xi and Duterte were talking about 'exploiting' the Spratlys at a meeting in Beijing when Xi made the comments, Philippine media say. China probably did not want the 'total war' comment disclosed and political experts say Beijing may speak more cautiously with Duterte's government in the future, or 'resort to more sinister means'. But analysts say Beijing will avoid any retaliation because it sees Duterte trying to improve relations after a 'rocky past filled with broken promises'. Duterte has visited China twice, and the two sides sat down this month to start working out their maritime differences, with China offering 'generous aid packages'.

'Sinisikap lang nilang mag-save ng mukha,' sabi ni Jay Batongbacal, direktor ng Institute for Maritime Affairs and Law of the Sea sa University of the Philippines. 'Ito ay isang tipikal na taktika ng Tsina upang takutin ang mga kalapit na bansa.' Sinasakop ng Beijing ang halos 90 porsiyento ng South China Sea, kabilang ang Spratlys, na mayaman sa 'mga yaman na hindi pa nagagamit at mga nakatagong kayamanan'.
